title: Record-to-Record Comparator: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Record-to-Record Comparator does and why archives need it. A record-to-record comparator puts two records side by side and lists every difference: which fields changed, which were added, which were removed. It is the 'spot the difference' game played perfectly, field by field. Nothing slips past it.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

title: How the Record-to-Record Comparator works
description: Overview: what the Record-to-Record Comparator does and why archives need it. Real comparators align two records field by field, classify each field as unchanged, modified, added, or removed, and score overall similarity with weighted field matching (a title change matters more than a whitespace change). Text fields get word-level diffs, numeric fields get delta values, and list fields get set-difference analysis. The output is a structured change report with before/after values per field.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Record-to-Record Comparator works: the deep tour
title: How the Record-to-Record Comparator works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Record-to-Record Comparator does and why archives need it. Real comparators align two records field by field, classify each field as unchanged, modified, added, or removed, and score overall similarity with weighted field matching (a title change matters more than a whitespace change). Text fields get word-level diffs, numeric fields get delta values, and list fields get set-difference analysis. The output is a structured change report with before/after values per field. Advanced comparators handle schema drift (the same field renamed between versions), normalize values before comparing (dates in different formats), and distinguish meaningful changes from formatting noise. Quality is measured by diff accuracy on versioned record pairs and by false-change rate on identical records. The limits are semantic equivalence ('NYC' vs 'New York City'), which needs the synonym registry rather than raw comparison — the comparator flags likely-equivalents instead of declaring them different.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.
